tagline: Back roads through Londonderry's apple country.
intro: The Apple Way starts on Gilcreast Road by the Londonderry Town Offices and wanders about ten miles of town roads, Pillsbury, High Range, Elwood and Adams, before it finishes on Mammoth Road. The Visit NH trip sheet lists orchards and farms, churches and old schoolhouses along the way, the schoolhouses by number, and the site of the Wycoff Palm Leaf Hat Factory on Adams Road.

Families from Ireland and New England settled here in April 1719, and that year the first potato in North America was grown in what is now Derry, then part of the town. The town was chartered in 1722 and named for Londonderry in Ulster. Today it is known for its apple orchards.
season: Visit NH's Apple Way trip sheet calls late summer through fall prime time for picking apples.

moments.title: Dutton Farm
moments.text: The trip sheet points to the old sugar shack behind the barn at the town's first maple syrup producer, and says the sugar maples here are still tapped every spring.

moments.title: High Range Road
moments.text: The trip sheet sends the road past Jackson Hall, which began as Bell Tavern, to Sunnycrest Farm, where visitors pick their own apples, strawberries and blueberries.

moments.title: Mack's Orchards, Mammoth Road
moments.text: On Mammoth Road, the last of the way, the trip sheet lists School House #2, the Reverend William Morrison's old meeting house and Mack's Orchards on Moose Hill, a stop for apples and cider.
